subject: Resilient bridge backpressure probe: Pinecone + S3 fallback POC
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@pinecone.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: samir@atlasdata.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call last week. We sketched a short technical probe that simulates write and query bursts and verifies safe fallthrough to S3-backed vectors for long-tail data. High level: run 72-hour synthetic bursts, measure P95 latency and cold-miss cost delta, and validate automated rehydration behavior.

Attaching a 1-pager test plan (resilient_bridge_testplan.pdf). Would Redwood be open to a joint 2-week POC that (a) wires up Pinecone as the hot index, (b) configures S3 as the cold lane, and (c) runs 3 scaled bursts (10k qps peak) to stress backpressure/failover?

We can provide a sandbox Pinecone project and an AtlasData connector instance. Pricing for the sandbox is on us; we just need an engineer to help with routing + fallback hooks on Redwood.

—Alice
Solutions Engineer, Pinecone

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Team — forwarding Pinecone's ask. This is different from our typical connector onboarding: they want a resilience-focused probe specifically around backpressure and S3 fallthrough. Key asks: two-week POC, Redwood engineer to wire routing/fallback, and joint test runs at 10k qps peak.

My quick thoughts: we should scope the engineering effort, confirm we can simulate 10k qps safely in sandbox (no noisy neighbour risk), and capture measurable acceptance criteria (latency, successful rehydrations, cost delta). Ben/Vanessa — can you review the attached test plan and suggest any missing telemetry we need in Console? Aditya — will this require any runtime changes or can we implement as an orchestration + policy on top of existing connector logic?

Thanks — K
Kimberly Park
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Kimberly,

Looks feasible but a couple of flags:
- 10k qps peak is non-trivial; we'll need a dedicated sandbox GPU pool for the run windows to avoid impacting other teams. Estimate: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for burst windows (ephemeral) + a small staging PGVector for baseline comparisons.
- Telemetry: we should capture token-level cost, per-request routing decision, cache hit rate, rehydration time, and a backpressure/error signal stream (HTTP 429/503 rates). Add these to Console as a temporary dashboard.
- Failure modes: define acceptable SLA for fallthrough. I propose P95 < 250ms for hot hits, P95 < 1.2s for rehydrations, and successful rehydration >= 99% within 30 minutes.

I'll draft a minimal runbook and list of required infra artifacts.
Ben
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Adding commercial + partner ops notes:
- Commercial: ask Pinecone for a sandbox credit commit and a short commercial note confirming no bill to Redwood for usage during POC. We'll capture any exceptions if we need extended runs.
- Contract: we should get a quick mutual action plan (MAP) with defined deliverables and a basic NDAs/PO if they insist. Keep it lightweight.
- Go-to-market angle: if the probe proves the flow, we can offer a partner solution kit for customers with cold-tiering needs — coordinate with Solutions.

I'll own partner comms and the MAP draft.
—V
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@pinecone.io>, Samir Rao <samir@atlasdata.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Hi Alice / Samir — thanks, we like the probe concept and can commit to a 2-week joint POC window the week of May 17.

What we need from Pinecone/Atlas:
1) Sandbox project credentials by May 12.
2) A short MAP with deliverables and run windows (we'll circulate a one-page draft).
3) Test dataset and expected query distribution profiles you want to exercise (cold-tail vs. hot set).

From Redwood side: Ben will provision ephemeral GPUs and a staging connector. Vanessa will draft the MAP and confirm partner ops terms. Aditya — can you assess whether the routing + rehydration will require runtime changes or we can implement as a policy layer? Please advise by EOD Friday (May 7).

I'll attach the runbook outline and a capacity matrix in follow-up.

Best — K
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Alice Nguyen <alice@pinecone.io>, Samir Rao <samir@atlasdata.com>
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinecone x Redwood probe idea — S3 fallback under burst

Quick update after offline review:
- Routing/re-hydration approach: implementable today as an orchestration policy. We'll use an inference proxy rule that routes by vector-store affinity; on sustained queue depth > threshold, proxy will mark index shards as degraded and route to S3-cold read path. No kernel/runtime change required for the POC.
- Telemetry hooks: I will add a temporary event stream (routing_decision, cache_hit, rehydrate_start/complete, error_code) and wire it into a Console dashboard for the run. Ben — please share the GPU provisioning details (count + windows) and I will coordinate the test harness.
- Risk: rehydration latency depends heavily on object size and S3 egress throttling; we'll simulate a realistic distribution but advise a separate run for very large vectors (>2MB) if you want representative numbers.

Moving forward: I'll commit the orchestration policy and initial dashboard by Wed May 11.

—Aditya
Senior Staff Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
